newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 28.

text.p: Workers in Japan's automobile manufacturing industry are expected to work an average 30 hours more this year than last year, despite joint initiatives by unions and management to cut working hours. This is due to strong sales of recreational vehicles, and a trend of car makers' temporary workers leaving before their contracts expire and increasing the workload on the regular staff.

Ishikawajima-Harima Heavy Industries Co Ltd and Sumitomo Heavy Industries Ltd have agreed to exchange shipbuilding design data via computer to cut costs. The two companies plan to share design data on very large crude carriers (VLCC) of 200,000 tonnes or more, sharply reducing costs for design development, which constitute an estimated seven to eight percent of the ships' overall cost.
